chapter: The Washingtonians, Bechet and drum style
title: Admired drummers and how he developed his own style
summary: Greer praises Zutty, Baby Dodds, Catlett, Chick Webb and Kaiser Marshall, then says his style came from intuition, watching the Capitol Theatre drummer and the soloist's left hand; brushes at Gregory's.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Was there much -- what did you think of drummers like Baby Dodds, Zutty Singleton, did you hear him?

Zutty, well, Zutty was one of my best pals. Good drummer. Baby, good drummer. Good drummer. beautiful drummer. Sidney Catlett, /Chick Webb, beautiful drumer. Kaiser was a beautiful drummer. He fitted Fletcher's band like a glove. He used to tell everybody he was my brother.
How did you go about developing your style, because, you know, I have listened to --
You have a very unusual way of playing. A lot of times......
I can't truthfully say how I developed
my style. As I told you, I always got a lead sheet, a guide, and most of the things I do it was just intuition, like guys playing piano, things come to them. All right.
How can I say that. I used to love to go to the Capital Theatre and hear the symphony band play, because them guys are crack musicians. That was before the talkies, you know.

New York. Capitol Theatre. 50th Street and Broad. Big', and me and Duke used to go there to hear them play. To hell with the pictures, just to hear them guys play. That rhythm section, they was something. And the drummer, I forget his name, he used to do some things, man, so tricky, I would go see him 50 times and then I'd go on the job, I would fool around until I caughtit my way. I'd turned it around to me, not like he do it.

Same sound, but my idea, me. I would do that all the time. I ain't never told the guy show me how to do nothing. I go and sit and look at him. He'd do it two or three times, then while I'm getting paid on the job, I would try it, if it any good, I keep it. If it ain't no good, forget it. That's me, just my idea.
The guys say, 'How you do that,' and then I always, like me and Brooksie/play a lot of things, if I can see his
left hand, I can tell the way his hand moves, what he is going to do. As long as I can see him, I got him. I know what to do because I'm thinking way ahead of him. I got him. That's right.
I notice like on a lot of the recordings.
Yeah, I saw you at Gregory's a lot of time.

You noticed down at Gregory's very seldom I used -- very seldom you see me pick up the stick and come on out loud, brushes. Because I do the same thing with a brush, more I think, than I can with a drumstick.

Because I don't know what Brooks is going to play, but I'm looking right at him. I don't know what Procope going to play, until I hear him, so I place things that will come around and say, fill out and sound good A lot of guys would, 'How you do that?' favorite saying: I say, 'Man, I'm crazy.' Bubber Miley's -- 'How you doing, Bubber?' 'Man, I'm crazy, I don't know.' Bechet say, 'I'm crazy', that's all they ever say. Crazy like a fox. One of them things. Good times.
